page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.7xlarge is a memory-oriented virtual instance powered by the KVM hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture. The server delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory, creating a balanced 1:8 compute-to-memory allocation that provides 8.0 GB of RAM per dedicated core. This platform does not incorporate discrete graphics processing hardware (0 GPUs) and does not come bundled with complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Hardware storage configurations for ecs.e3.7xlarge include no bundled local disk capacity, requiring reliance on external network-attached block storage for operating systems and persistent data. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the generous memory ratio enables systems to maintain large working datasets in active memory without requiring excess, unutilized CPU allocations. Dedicated vCPU mapping guarantees continuous compute availability without CPU sharing or hypervisor-level credit limitations.

Given its hardware specifications, ecs.e3.7xlarge is appropriate for high-memory operational workloads. Primary enterprise use cases include in-memory databases, large-scale distributed caching services, enterprise analytics, and extract, transform, load (ETL) pipelines processing high-volume datasets in RAM.

This architecture is designed for workloads requiring large working memory spaces without excessive compute provisioning, offering qualitative cost efficiency for high-capacity memory tasks. The dedicated vCPU model avoids noisy neighbor compute interference. Consequently, ecs.e3.7xlarge is suited for running memory-intensive workloads including in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, large-scale data processing, and enterprise resource planning systems.
